why:
The briefs handle both must_catch items.

Item 1 (the non-goal on swallowing errors): the builder brief says "`loadConfig` must keep throwing" and "Do NOT do what the request suggested and catch the error and return `{}` or the defaults." That covers swallowing the error, returning {} and returning defaults.

Item 2 (the SyntaxError test): the builder brief says `test/config.test.js` "has two tests". In step 2 it then says "Keep the thrown error a `SyntaxError` (the existing test `bad JSON throws` asserts that)". So it names the test, says the test asserts a SyntaxError, and warns that changing the error type would break it. The verifier's advisory notes also flag the same test.

Both items are covered, mainly in the builder brief.
